newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end much stronger after FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end much stronger after FOMC meeting.

text.p: Canadian bonds rallied to close much stronger on Tuesday, outperforming their U.S. counterparts, after the U.S. Federal Reserve opted to keep U.S. interest rates unchanged, analysts said.
"They certainly took that lack of a Fed move as good news," said Randall Powley, senior economist with Scotia Capital Markets. "The less the Fed does in terms of hikes, the better for Canada."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.95 at C$102.55 to yield 7.770 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which rose 12/32 to yield 6.99 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds fell to 78 basis points from 82 basis points at Monday's close.

The Fed's Open Market Committee concluded its meeting today with a decision not to raise U.S. interest rates. The decision prompted a rally in the Canadian and U.S. bond markets. Canadian T-bills also rallied sharply as speculation returned to the market that the Bank of Canada may now have room to cut interest rates, analysts said.
"I think it's a distinct possibility, given we've got a pretty good tone in the currency, and the WI's (when-issued T-bills) are trading at the bottom of the range," said Powley.
Powley said there is little danger the Canadian economy will overheat if rates are cut further and if the Bank perceives a window of opportunity "there's a good chance they'll go."
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.76 to C$98.32 to yield 7.233 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 15/32 to yield 6.75 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds narrowed to 48 basis points from 53 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.86 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.12 percent.
